claims: He discusses the ethical conduct of the Jewish people during the conquest, saying "ethical conduct" is not mentioned as a topic, though specific laws and behaviors are discussed.
summary: Rabbi Tawil examines the second battle of the city of Ai in the book of Yehoshua, focusing on the strategic ambush commanded by Hashem and executed by Yehoshua. He discusses the partnership between divine assistance and human effort, the lessons regarding the spoils of war, and the ethical conduct of the Jewish people during the conquest.
questions: Why did the Jewish people lose the first battle against Ai?
Why did Hashem allow the Jewish people to take the spoils of war in the second battle but not the first?
What is the significance of Yehoshua raising his spear during the battle?
How did the Jewish people treat the king of Ai compared to ancient customs of warfare?
